source.topic: the last edition coming off the truck

candidates.text: Bledsoe claims the newsstand at 7:30 PM, which is when the last edition coming off the truck was on. Asked about it, Bledsoe cannot say that the late edition led with the bridge contract and not the hold-up — and everybody who was there can.
Marchetti still carries it: ink still wet enough to come off on a glove. The last edition coming off the truck was at 7:30 PM, at the newsstand.
The shift change at the garage was at 11:00 PM, and Rafferty was at the garage for it.
Rafferty still carries it: cylinder oil on a cuff. The shift change at the garage was at 11:00 PM, at the garage.
Found at the newsstand: A subpoena naming Kreuzer before the grand jury, with Bledsoe’s name written in the margin.
Feldman says Kreuzer said to Bledsoe that a man who testifies sleeps better.
Found at the suite: A promissory note for $4,000 signed by Thorndike, endorsed to Kreuzer, three months past due.
Bledsoe says Kreuzer told Thorndike that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Found at the suite: A draft codicil in Kreuzer’s hand striking Rafferty out of the will, dated last Tuesday and unsigned.
Carbone says Kreuzer told Rafferty the lawyer was coming Thursday and that the arrangement would be changed.
Marchetti hired us, and wants it known that Bledsoe needed the victim silent, and would rather we started there.
Steinbach on Dandridge: Dandridge sends money out of every pay envelope and cannot say where it goes.
Marchetti on Dandridge: A woman at Mrs. Teague’s asked for Dandridge by a name Dandridge has not used in years.
Rafferty on Dandridge: Dandridge keeps a photograph and will not be asked about it twice.
A board-and-keep receipt at Mrs. Teague’s, monthly, eight years of them.
A child’s shoe at Mrs. Teague’s, and nobody at Mrs. Teague’s has any children.
The woman who keeps the child says it straight out: Dandridge was at Mrs. Teague’s from 8:00 PM to 8:30 PM, the same as every week, and left with the same face as always.
The parish register at Mrs. Teague’s has the christening in it, and the board money receipted through the evening in question.
Kessler on Marchetti: Marchetti was carrying a parcel into the newsstand and came out without it.
Carbone on Marchetti: There is a man who meets people at the newsstand and nobody will say his name out loud.
Dandridge on Marchetti: Marchetti has been selling things that were never Marchetti’s to sell.
Wrapping paper and a cut string at the newsstand, and the shop it came from closed two years ago.
A pawn ticket at the newsstand in a name that does not exist, made out at the hour in question.
The receiver at the newsstand would rather talk than be held: Marchetti was there from 9:30 PM handing over a parcel of somebody else’s silver, which is a charge Marchetti will take over this one.
The goods turn up, tagged and dated, and the tag puts Marchetti at the newsstand from 9:30 PM with both hands full.

The goods turn up, tagged and dated, and the tag puts Thorndike at the El platform from 9:30 PM to 10:00 PM with both hands full.
Steinbach on Salerno: Salerno was asking around for a hundred dollars in a hurry earlier in the week.
Marchetti on Salerno: A man nobody knew was waiting for Salerno at the newsstand and would not give a name.
Rafferty on Salerno: Salerno goes very quiet when the racing wire is mentioned.
Betting slips at the newsstand in Salerno’s pocketbook, all of them losers, all of them this month.
A book of markers at the newsstand with Salerno’s initials against four of them.
The bookmaker’s runner is found and will say it: Salerno was at the newsstand from 8:00 PM paying off eleven hundred dollars, a dollar at a time, and went nowhere near the killing.
The book at the newsstand has the payment entered against Salerno’s name and the time beside it, from 8:00 PM, in the clerk’s own hand.
Thorndike on Rafferty: Rafferty had taken a drink and had gone to some trouble about the smell of it.
Feldman on Rafferty: Rafferty is on a temperance pledge that Rafferty mentions before anybody asks.
Steinbach on Rafferty: Somebody at Mrs. Teague’s says Rafferty is in more often than Rafferty lets on.
A bottle at Mrs. Teague’s pushed behind the pipes, the seal broken and the level down.
A tab at Mrs. Teague’s in a name that is not Rafferty’s, in Rafferty’s handwriting.
The man behind the counter at Mrs. Teague’s knows exactly: Rafferty was on the same stool from 6:00 PM to 6:30 PM and was in no condition to walk anywhere, let alone do this.
The tab at Mrs. Teague’s is dated and timed, from 6:00 PM to 6:30 PM, and Rafferty was there to run it up.
